data.targetWord: The ultimate reality and source of all existence in Hindu thought — infinite and beyond full human comprehension

examples.en-GB: Some Hindus see Brahman as an impersonal cosmic principle; others as a personal God.

data.targetWord: The individual soul or true inner self — eternal, it does not die when the body dies

examples.en-GB: The atman is the true self — it passes through the cycle of samsara until moksha is achieved.

data.targetWord: The moral law of cause and effect — actions and their consequences across lifetimes, shaped by intention

examples.en-GB: Good intentions and actions create positive karma; harmful actions create negative karma.

data.targetWord: Right conduct, duty, and cosmic order — living according to your role and the moral law

examples.en-GB: Following one's dharma — one's duty and role — creates good karma.

data.targetWord: The cycle of birth, death, and rebirth — the soul passes through many lives until liberation is achieved

examples.en-GB: The atman passes through many lives in samsara, shaped by karma, until moksha is reached.

data.targetWord: Liberation from the cycle of samsara — the ultimate spiritual goal in Hinduism

examples.en-GB: Moksha can be pursued through devotion, knowledge, or ethical action depending on the tradition.

data.targetWord: Non-violence — the principle of not causing harm to any living being; a core Hindu ethical value

examples.en-GB: Ahimsa motivates vegetarianism and peaceful conflict resolution in Hindu life.

data.targetWord: An act of devotion and worship, offering items such as flowers, incense, and food to a deity

examples.en-GB: Daily puja at a home shrine might involve flowers, incense, water, and a lamp.

data.targetWord: A Hindu temple — understood as the home of the deity, whose murti is treated as a living presence

examples.en-GB: In the mandir, the pujari performs elaborate puja for the deity multiple times each day.

data.targetWord: A sacred image or statue of a Hindu deity, treated as the actual presence of that deity

examples.en-GB: The murti is bathed, dressed, and given offerings as if honouring a royal guest.

data.targetWord: The waving of a flame before a deity during puja — a moment of warmth, light, and divine connection

examples.en-GB: During aarti, worshippers hold their hands over the flame and touch their eyes, receiving the deity's blessing.

data.targetWord: Food or offerings blessed in puja and then distributed to worshippers as a sharing in the deity's blessing

examples.en-GB: Receiving prasad is a way of sharing in the deity's blessing and grace.

data.targetWord: The auspicious 'seeing' of a deity and receiving the deity's gaze during worship at a mandir

examples.en-GB: Pilgrims travel great distances to receive darshan at famous temples.

data.targetWord: A form or incarnation that a deity — especially Vishnu — takes on earth at times of need

examples.en-GB: Rama and Krishna are both avatars of Vishnu, who descended to restore dharma on earth.

data.targetWord: The 'Song of God' — a Hindu scripture in which Krishna teaches Arjuna about duty, devotion, and right action

examples.en-GB: The Bhagavad Gita is one of the most widely read Hindu scriptures worldwide.

data.targetWord: The epic story of Rama, Sita, and the defeat of Ravana — a story of dharma, duty, and loyalty

examples.en-GB: The Ramayana is the source story behind Diwali, celebrating Rama's return home.

data.targetWord: The Festival of Lights — associated with Rama's return and the blessings of Lakshmi; celebrates the victory of good over evil

examples.en-GB: At Diwali, homes are lit with diyas (clay lamps), fireworks are set off, and puja is performed for Lakshmi.

data.targetWord: The spring festival of colours celebrating joy, love, and the victory of devotion over evil

examples.en-GB: At Holi, people throw coloured powder and water, and celebrate the defeat of the demoness Holika.

data.targetWord: A sacred word, syllable, or phrase used in prayer and meditation — 'Om' is the most sacred

examples.en-GB: 'Om' is the most sacred mantra, representing Brahman — the ultimate reality.

data.targetWord: The elephant-headed deity associated with wisdom, new beginnings, and the removal of obstacles

examples.en-GB: Ganesha is widely worshipped at the start of new ventures, journeys, and important events.

data.targetWord: The preserver and sustainer deity in Hinduism, associated with love and mercy; takes avatars when the world needs protecting

examples.en-GB: Vishnu's ten main avatars include Rama and Krishna, who both restored dharma on earth.

data.targetWord: The deity of destruction and transformation in Hinduism — destruction that enables renewal and creation

examples.en-GB: Shiva is associated with meditation, yoga, and the cosmic dance (Nataraja).

data.targetWord: The oldest Hindu scriptures — believed to be eternal truths revealed to sages; written in Sanskrit

examples.en-GB: The Vedas contain hymns, rituals, and philosophical speculation and are the foundation of Hindu tradition.

data.targetWord: The Eternal Way or Eternal Truth — the name many Hindus prefer for their tradition, suggesting its principles are timeless

examples.en-GB: Sanatana Dharma suggests the principles of Hinduism are eternal, not founded at a particular historical moment.

data.targetWord: A Hindu temple priest who performs puja and ritual worship on behalf of the community

examples.en-GB: The pujari performs elaborate puja for the murti several times daily at the mandir.

data.title: Order the Hindu spiritual journey from atman through to moksha
items: Atman — the individual soul enters the cycle of samsara
Karma — actions shape the quality of the next life
Dharma — following one's duty creates good karma
Samsara — the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth continues
Moksha — liberation from samsara; the atman returns to Brahman

data.title: Order the steps of a typical home puja
items: Prepare the shrine — place flowers, incense, and water
Ring a bell to invite the deity's attention
Offer flowers, incense, and water to the murti
Perform aarti — wave the lamp before the deity
Receive prasad — blessed food shared with the family

data.title: Order the Hindu sacred texts from oldest to most recent in tradition
items: Vedas — oldest scriptures; hymns and philosophy
Upanishads — philosophical discussions on Brahman and atman
Ramayana — epic story of Rama and Sita
Mahabharata — great epic including the Bhagavad Gita
Bhagavad Gita — Krishna's teaching on duty and devotion
